label: Oven wire rack
test_scope: Offline synthetic tests. Forces and mass are engineering assumptions, not hardware measurements.
physics_source: Generated from model.json and convex collision pieces
physics_notes:
# oven_wire_rack — repaired realism review

Evidence: f3459, f3483, f3525.

Changes:

- Matched visible 17 longitudinal wires
- Replaced eight coarse collision wires with all 23 cylindrical members
- Warm heat-discolored metal
- Two shared instances retained
- Round 2: reevaluated wire geometry in open cavity after removing erroneous ceiling occlusion; retained two shared instances
- Round 2: slide direction follows shared fitted rack orientation and the reconstructed support runners

Current geometry: 1012 triangles; 23 convex contact pieces. Physical size (local bounds): [0.67, 0.504, 0.0103] m.

Physics: Circular rod-volume budget: 17 x 0.494 m x pi x (0.0023 m)^2 plus 2.316 m x pi x (0.004 m)^2 plus 1.32 m x pi x (0.0028 m)^2, times 7850 kg/m3, is 2.27 kg; about 0.02 kg is shared at welded overlaps. Use 2.25 kg. Actual product weight and wire diameters remain unmeasured.

Seventeen longitudinal wires, four perimeter bars and two cross-supports each have matching cylindrical collision geometry. Both instances share visual topology; their positions/orientations use front-rail fits, stored in evidence/qa_rack_fit.json. The wire-envelope score is intentionally distinguished from fine-wire alignment.

Remaining limitations:

- Rack underside bends and removable rail lift behavior not recovered
- Envelope IoU is not fine-wire overlap; per-wire alignment still assessed visually
- Travel and mass estimated, not measured

Calibrated images are 1280 x 1707 undistorted source frames. Review renders use the same intrinsics and cam_from_world matrices, downsampled to 640 x 854 with the original pixel aspect. WORLD is metric Z-up; glTF exports Y-up. Intrinsics and camera poses were not adjusted to improve scores. The three open views use a shared +0.7 EV exposure correction to approximate the source phone's auto-exposure; this is an estimated review lighting setting. Manual source masks have approximately 2-5 review-pixel edge uncertainty; they are agent annotations, not independent human ground truth. Rack IoU measures the combined outer envelope, not individual wire pixel agreement. LAB histograms use only common projected source/render pixels, with photographed occluders excluded. Lighting and reflections are estimated, not measured BRDFs.

Physics masses, COM, friction, restitution and textile parameters are explicitly estimated; exact product identity and measured weights are unavailable. A/B grades do not certify dynamics or unobserved geometry. No drawer/rack movement or hood filter removal was demonstrated. The oven door alone uses measured sparse hinge angles (confidence 0.45), f3459 was corrected to 0.621537 rad from the photographed handle position, and f3525 reuses the nearby full-open angle. Rest pose remains a best fit to the calibrated reconstruction, whose depth/pose errors do not permit a tape-measure accuracy claim.

The MuJoCo XML is a contact/kinematic check harness with flat-colored proxy visuals. Appearance is reviewed using the textured Blender assets and embedded GLB materials; the XML is not the photorealistic appearance deliverable.

Rebuild this type with its build.py under Blender. Rebuild and review the whole set with build_all.py. Shared implementation is asset_builder.py, persistent physics/instance metadata is qa_metadata.py, source annotations are evidence/qa_mask_annotations.json, and source measurements are evidence/qa_depth_rectangles.json. Texture generation is not rerun during builds; its output and prompt are packaged. The existing reconstruction replay remains at ../../layout/replay/index.html.
